finding.claim: purge handler discards the result of checkPerm, so the admin permission check is never enforced. Any caller who reaches the handler can run purgeAll. The sibling rotateKeys correctly uses mustPerm and returns on failure.
finding.source: Any authenticated low-privilege user (the User from request context) sends a request to the purge route

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the user from request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is ignored; there is no return or abort
Sibling rotateKeys uses mustPerm and returns when the check fails, which shows the intended pattern

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm result is unused. No other auth check exists in the file. The route table and middleware are not in the repo (only handlers.go exists), so I could not confirm any upstream admin middleware. Within the code present, the control is not enforced.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12-14 returns a bool that is discarded at line 26; no middleware or route table in repo, only handlers.go exists)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u,"admin") as a bare statement, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user, unlike rotateKeys at handlers.go:33-35, which tests mustPerm and returns on failure; upstream middleware can't be seen, but within the code present nothing blocks a low-privilege user.
